author: evergreen reporter
title: St. Louis County man receives 22-year sentence for shooting at police
text:
A man from Breckenridge Hills, Missouri, was sentenced to 22 years in prison for shooting at multiple St. Louis County police officers in 2024. U.S. District Judge John A. Ross handed down the sentence on Tuesday.
Dylan Farmer, 21, pleaded guilty in June to four counts of assaulting a law enforcement officer and two counts of discharging a firearm during a crime of violence. According to court documents, Farmer fired first at officers with the St. Louis County Police Department Special Response Unit (SRU) as they attempted to locate an individual wanted in connection with a double homicide.
On February 13, 2024, officers found a vehicle linked to the wanted person parked on Virginia Avenue in St. Louis. When Farmer unlocked and entered the vehicle, police moved in to detain him. Officers wore vests labeled “Police,” and three vehicles had blue flashing emergency lights. The officers were also task force members with the U.S. Marshals Service and FBI.
As three officers approached in their SUV, Farmer opened fire using a .45-caliber semiautomatic handgun equipped with a 50-round drum magazine, damaging the police SUV. Officers returned fire while Farmer fled across the street and between buildings, firing another shot at an officer before running down an alley and shooting multiple times at another officer who took cover behind a dumpster.
Farmer then hid on the porch of a house on Alaska Avenue. When spotted by police driving down the street, he fired again and damaged their vehicle before surrendering after being wounded by return fire from officers. Officers provided medical assistance until an ambulance arrived.
One officer sustained an eye injury when glass flew into his eye after a bullet ricocheted off a car window; another suffered an ankle injury while seeking cover.
The case was investigated by the St. Louis County Police Department, FBI, St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department, and U.S. Marshals Service. Assistant U.S. Attorney Paul D’Agrosa prosecuted the case.
